- dbe-tool profile output looks COLD. Use the warm JSON trick.
- No PK/UNIQUE constraints in the schema.

## How to get full operator timings
- dbe-tool sql "<warm q>; <warm q>; SET enable_profiling='json'; SET profiling_output='/home/shresth/dev/db_evolve/work/slots/slot0/.dbe/scratch_x.json'; <q>" then Grep '"operator_timing"|"operator_name"|"operator_cardinality"|"latency"|"Dynamic Filters"'. /tmp is NOT readable. Compare "latency" too: CPU alone hides serial phases.
- A/B in one session: CREATE TEMP VIEW va/vb, then `from va; from vb;` x3, then profile each into a separate file.

## Key finding: CM on join keys blocks the BF
- physical_hash_join.cpp FinalizeFilters: BF only if !has_cast && no storage_offset, except an exact BF through the offset on cond 0 (E0021). A hashed BF is never pushed through an offset.
- Exact BF: TrySetExactBloomFilter (:970) caps EXACT_BF_MAX_BITS_PER_KEY=128, EXACT_BF_SMALL_RANGE=1<<22, MAX_RANGE=1<<32. Hashed BF: 12 bits/key.
- PushRangeSetFilter (gap-split ranges) only for 50 < keys <= 3200.

## Measurement lessons
- The first 2-3 runs of a query in a process are slow (~2x warm-up). Alternate A/B/A/B.
- Do NOT wrap in count(*): it changes the plan. Use a temp view + `from v`.
- dbe-tool bash: no pipes, no shell variables, no $(...).
- Bench noise is ±10-20% per template (q19, q08, q03, q14 worst).
- In long bench sequences q18 is ~10% slower after q09/q13 (artifact).

- q03: lineitem scan 2.24s CPU, HJ on l_orderkey 0.75s.
- q18: 15M-group agg dominates (exhausted).

- FSST DecompressVector path is not hot.

1. (dispatched r9) a larger exact BF cap.
2. Check whether the q03/q07/q08/q21 hashed BFs would go exact under the new cap; if not, consider exact BFs for clustered probes regardless of range.
3. HJ build/probe throughput on large regular builds (q05 orderkey HJ ~150ns/probe row).
4. q07: gate the offset BF when the scan already has a selective BF (only if q07 gets flagged).
5. MARK delim joins (IN/EXISTS in OR) via the deliminator: check the NULL semantics.

- Rule order: src/optimizer/optimizer.cpp. Scan-filter cardinality: RelationStatisticsHelper::InspectTableFilter.
- Deliminator: src/optimizer/deliminator.cpp: SelectionIsReplaceableByJoinFilter (SEMI+ANTI now), ConvertNotDistinctToEqual, SubqueryIsSimple.
- Join filter generation: JoinFilterPushdownOptimizer::GenerateJoinFilters. NDF conds are skipped. DELIM_GET build => build_side_has_filter.
- Perfect HJ: perfect_hash_join_executor.cpp (CanDoPerfectHashJoin, FullScanHashTable, PerfectHashJoinBuildEvent since E0024). Perfect HA: plan_aggregate.cpp. FSST: src/storage/compression/fsst.cpp.

issues.title: Exact BF bitmap up to 2^27 bits when 1024 bits/key allows
issues.hypothesis: In q05 the lineitem scan is the hottest operator: 0.92s CPU out of about 1.7s total, 60M rows in and 2.03M out. Its join filter is a HASHED BF over 455k o_orderkey values spread across a 60M range. TrySetExactBloomFilter (physical_hash_join.cpp:1011) caps the exact bitmap at count*128 = 58.3M bits, so this range (59.99M) misses the cap by 3%. I ran a measured A/B with no code change: I widened the orders date window by about 2 weeks, giving ~500k keys, which is enough to cross the cap. The lineitem scan dropped 0.92s -> 0.48s CPU (-48%) even though more rows qualify, and false positives went away (1.99M -> exact 1.88M rows, where the hashed BF let ~10% extra rows through). q05-shaped wall time fell from 331/256/266ms to 244/229/208/230ms (~-15%). An exact bitmap probe costs one bit test with no hashing. The probe keys (lineitem l_orderkey) come in clustered order, so even a multi-MB bitmap stays cache-friendly. Note: an earlier memory entry said raising this cap was low value because it removed only ~10% of rows. That looked at rows only; the CPU saving comes from the cheaper probe.
issues.plan: In src/execution/operator/join/physical_hash_join.cpp, TrySetExactBloomFilter (lines ~1009-1016): keep the 128 bits/key rule and the EXACT_BF_SMALL_RANGE floor, and add a mid tier. The exact bitmap is also allowed if range < MinValue(EXACT_BF_MID_RANGE = 1<<27 bits (16MB), ht.Count() * 1024). In code: key_cap = MaxValue(key_cap, MinValue<idx_t>(EXACT_BF_MID_RANGE, ht.Count()*1024)). Keep the EXACT_BF_MAX_RANGE guard and update the comment that says memory is bounded by the pointer table. Check that the bitmap allocation and zeroing in SetExactRange (bloom filter class) works for 16MB, that the build-side insert for exact mode is thread-safe for the larger size (it is already used up to 2^32 ranges with dense keys), and that the E0021 offset path calls the same function. Validate with the q05 A/B above: o_orderdate < '1995-12-25' (hashed today) must become exact, and the lineitem scan CPU should drop to about 0.48s. Results must match the old build.
issues.expected_gain: q05 -10..-15% (scan CPU -48%). Possibly q03/q07/q08/q21/q18, where sparse orderkey/custkey/partkey BFs sit between 128 and 1024 bits/key over ranges up to 134M. Geomean maybe -1..-2%.
issues.generality: Any FK join where a filtered dimension or fact (orders by date, customers by segment) builds a BF on a key range of up to ~134M values at 0.1-1% density. This is very common for star/snowflake date-filtered joins. Queries that could get slower are those with random (unclustered) probe keys against a 4-16MB bitmap: L3 misses there instead of an L2-resident hashed BF. The 1024 bits/key bound limits that to at most 128 bytes of bitmap per build key. There is also a one-time zeroing cost of up to 16MB per join.
issues.risk: Low. This only changes a threshold on an existing, verified mechanism. The main risks are random-probe cache behaviour and memory per concurrent join.
